question: Why do crews weld rail at its neutral temperature?
answer: A rail has no stress at its neutral temperature. Welding it there means it starts out relaxed, with no force locked in as it cools. That's why crews in a German summer weld at night.
move: Join the rail when it is stress-free, so cooling locks in no force.

web.label: Card asking why crews weld rail at its neutral temperature. Two choices: wait an hour for a summer rail to cool, or weld now. Choosing to weld at neutral shows a relaxed rail with zero stress.
